summary: A qualifying run may begin at the final possible window, while the fixed ten-digit alphabet and fixed window length leave no meaningful intermediate asymptotic class between direct inspection and linear time.

optimality.argument: On an input with no three-equal run, changing any uninspected region, including the last three positions, can introduce the only qualifying triple or a larger triple than all earlier candidates. A correct worst-case algorithm must therefore inspect linearly many characters. Directly checking each constant-size window performs O(n) work and meets this adversarial inspection lower bound.

replacement_checks.evidence: The only or largest good integer can occur in the final length-three window, so an algorithm cannot certify the answer from a proper fixed prefix.
The reference examines each of n-2 windows with a constant number of character comparisons and stores one best digit.
Authored cases cover no candidate, zero with leading zeroes, exact length, overlapping windows, longer runs, multiple candidate digits, late maxima, and repeated maxima.
